rubric_notes: Correct release, families a.22.1.1-a.22.1.4 with sunids and members supported by the search evidence; superfamily = common origin, family = closer; TAFs explicitly not assigned nucleosomal function; keyword-only enzyme hits and j.63 peptide fragment handled well; limits and external-evidence needs stated. Flaw: declares H-NS proteins 'functional analogues... not homologs of histones' and H1/H5 relation 'functional, not fold-level' as flat assertions; SCOPe placement in a different fold does not establish non-homology or analogy. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct sccs, sunids, boundaries, family, protein and species labels (resolve calls in bundle; additional labels are accurate SCOPe 2.08 facts). States superfamily-level remote homology, no family-level or orthologous claim, and lists conclusions that overreach: HisE activity for d1vmga_, assuming MazG-like is a bona fide MazG enzyme, shared substrate/catalytic residues, whole-protein inference, template use. Names external evidence. No must_avoid violation.

Correct families c.55.1.1/.3/.4 within c.55.1, fold c.55, release 2.08, all supported by the releases and search responses. States superfamily-level homology of the catalytic cores with a conserved nucleotide/phosphate architecture, and rejects shared substrate, reaction, regulation, role, mechanism transfer, and whole-protein inference. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct hierarchy (a.25 fold, a.25.1 superfamily 47240, families 47241/47253/100951 with protein node 47263); fold vs superfamily distinction stated; superfamily read as common ancestry of the dimetal scaffold with functional divergence; explicit no-transfer rule; R1 correctly placed outside a.25.1; external evidence listed (assays, metal content, spectroscopy, mutagenesis). Factual: family/superfamily sunids are supported via search-result parents, but the release labels '2.08-stable' and periodic update '2.08-2026-08-16' are asserted without any release endpoint in the bundle.

Correct family/superfamily/fold placements with sunids, superfamily read as probable common evolutionary origin, copper and electron transfer kept family-specific, requires metal-binding/redox data or ligand-residue analysis, notes b.18.1.4 receptor confusion. Cites /api/v1/releases/current and sunid 49504, neither of which is in the evidence bundle (only four default-release searches), and asserts SCOPe 'carries no functional annotation' without retrieving the family comments. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families/superfamily/fold with sunids and example proteins supported by the bundle; correctly rejects conjugation, Ras-GTP and p97/VCP transfers. Decisive error: 'Ontology caveat' claims ubiquitin itself is filed only as k.45.1.1 and not under d.15.1, and builds unsafe-transfer point (5) on that. Ubiquitin is protein node 54238 in d.15.1.1; its own ubiquitin search hits are d.15.1.1 domains. Materially wrong relationship-bearing classification (bio <= 2). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Correct superfamily-level inference: c.23.1.1, c.23.1.4, c.23.1.5 share c.23.1; superfamily supports common origin, fold alone would not; distinct families so no function transfer. Rejects phosphorylation signaling, ODC-wing catalysis (major domain c.67.1.5), and KaiA clock/KaiC function; notes the KaiA C-terminal domain is a different fold. Identifier slip: gives the KaiA family sunid as 82345 (that is the protein node; the family is 82344). 'Current release' claim not in the evidence bundle.

Correct 2.08 placement in b.84.5 within fold b.84, sibling superfamilies named, family b.84.5.1 holding V1 (310706) and A1 (310707) nodes. Distinguishes architectural fold claim from superfamily homology claim and limits function transfer and scope to the bulge domain. Could have stated more explicitly that no non-homology claim is made toward b.84.1-b.84.4, but does not assert one. Release facts supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct f.21 fold and f.21.1/f.21.2/f.21.3 placement with sunids and family 81373/103502, bundle-supported; useful disambiguation of a.24 cytochrome b562, a.3.1.8 SoxA and the flavoprotein 'fumarate reductase' nodes. Requires independent sequence/structure evidence and rejects function/template transfer. However it states the split 'means the three groups are not homologous by SCOPe's criteria', treating separate superfamilies as a non-homology finding rather than absence of a positive assertion, and omits the f.21.3 possible-link curator note. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct c.2.1 superfamily placement and family sunids; protein nodes 51901, 63945, 75122 and the b.35.1.2 N-terminal ADH domain are supported by the search results in the bundle. Reads relationship as deep superfamily-level homology with divergent function, denies shared ligand/catalysis, flags pretrained-knowledge statements, and lists unsafe transfers (ligand, template, sequence-identity) plus required experimental evidence. The periodic-update label is not in this bundle but is accurate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct same-family conclusion with family SUNID 100905 and protein nodes (correct, though bundle contains only resolve responses). States 'family membership is a classification of common evolutionary origin, so SCOPe does treat these two as homologous' before caveating on designed proteins. Never mentions the 'not a true family' annotation. Bio capped at 2; factual 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete: 1.69 d1t1ja_ (sunid 106249) c.137.1.1 in its own fold c.137, no shared fold/superfamily with 1f8y; 2.08 d1t1ja1 A:1-118 c.23.14.2 in superfamily c.23.14 N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like within fold c.23, d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 in both releases. States shared superfamily = probable common origin and different family = distant relationship, explicitly structure-based classification change not evidence of NDT function; notes fragment l.1.1.1 domains. All claims supported by evidence bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identification: d1a14h2 sunid 343393, l.1.1.1, class l artifacts, Synthetic (311501) and N-terminal Tags (310894), d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1. Rejects fold/superfamily/family assignment, template selection, and function transfer from tag matches with sound reasoning. However the answer claims an API lookup of 1a14 domains and node lineage, while the bundle contains only the releases list, so these release-specific claims are not evidenced by cited records (though all are accurate).

Reasoning is strong: 1.75 whole-chain unit, 2.08 split into b.179.1.1 and f.60.1.1 with correct boundaries, domain-not-chain inference, caution against assuming cross-module homology, good search guidance. But its bundle contains only the 1.75 single-domain record, so the central 2.08 split and boundaries are API-dependent claims without supporting evidence; 2.04 split release not identified.

All five boundaries and SCCS correct; d.394.1.1 A:47-697 identified as new fold; four others tied to existing superfamilies; mosaic stated with function-transfer limits. Imprecision: says relationships are 'at superfamily level, not family level' and calls the bromodomain link superfamily-level, although d3jb9a4 sits in the shared Bromodomain family a.29.2.1 with CBP/GCN5/p300/TAF1. SIDs not named. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Explains repeat-module homology and that length tracks repeat count, with good RVD/function caveats; search bundle usefully shows many a.298.1.1 members of varying boundaries. Omits the decisive 're' heterogeneity annotation and representative repeat unit, and asserts '2.08 current release' without a releases endpoint in its bundle.

Correct metadata supported by bundle; cites 2.08-stable as base and records the dated periodic version actually used, with an accurate OpenAPI citation that dated selectors do not promise immutable snapshots. Correctly says the periodic label is not a new release number. Does not state that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable-release domains. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct a.47.2.1 placement for all chains, correct hierarchy, correct 1dn1 obsolescence and d3c98b_ (sunid 173092). Useful points on not double-counting 1ez3 copies and the superseded entry. However it claims 'Fragment status is not confirmed by SCOPe' because it never retrieved annotations; SCOPe does flag these domains with the fragment comment and 'ms' inconsistency, so the decisive annotation was ignored (ceiling 2). Misses the fragment-driven resemblance/resolution point. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Asserts that shared NAD(P) binding across c.2, c.3 and b.43 'is best classed as convergent at the fold level' because SCOPe did not place them together, treating absence of a positive assertion as evidence of independent origin; no alternative explanation offered. Divergence within c.2.1, short-motif and cofactor-switch caveats, and required evidence (topology, profile/HMM, superfamily assignment) are present, and function transfer across folds is rejected. Node sunids verified; release metadata and failed-search claims are not in the bundle.

States different folds in 2.04, shared superfamily b.18.1 in 2.08 with distinct families, probable common ancestry superfamily-level, no shared function. Correctly flags the d1nqdb2 l.1.1.1 artifact warning, which its bundle supports. All must_avoid satisfied.

Family-level homology correctly retained and sequence comparison from retrieved sequences is sound, but the answer never retrieved the annotations or homology endpoints, so it claims hf could not be found and advises not using hf for inclusion/exclusion decisions, contradicting the required 'retain and stratify' treatment and omitting the hf meaning (different fold despite similar sequence/SSE count). Hard ceiling for not engaging the decisive heterogeneous-fold annotation applies. Claims about 1ztr being an NMR folding-intermediate L16A mutant and 1p7j a K52E crystal structure are attributed to 'PDB metadata from the 2.08 API' but no such response is in the evidence bundle. Classification, sunids, sequences and boundaries are supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Lineage, sunids, boundaries, sequences and release are correct and bundle-supported. However the answer asserts 'the live 2.08 records carry no fragment flag' and 'the API does not corroborate a fragment annotation' after querying only search and sequence endpoints, never the annotations/homology endpoints where the fr inconsistency is recorded. Treating the fragment label as unverified and recommending representative selection 'by sequence-identity clustering on the full domains, not by the fragment label' effectively uses d1o5dt2 as a full-domain candidate (must_avoid) and ignores a decisive fragment annotation (hard ceiling bio <= 2). Fragment-aware alignment advice is given only conditionally; family diversity counts both as full lineages with no fragment stratification. Omits the fr semantics entirely.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Level-by-level semantics correct; new superfamily as the smallest claim consistent with evidence; new fold only if resemblance is weak or local; quantify resemblance, remote-homology search, no function transfer, provisional. All must_include met. Release context (2.08-stable, 2.08-2026-08-16) asserted with an empty evidence bundle.

Correctly places PI3K catalytic domain d.144.1.4 (56171) and APH d.144.1.6 (64411) under superfamily d.144.1 (56112) in release 2.08, and correctly notes the PI3K helical domain a.118.1.6 is a separate fold. However it gives the canonical protein kinase family as 'd.144.1.2' from pretrained knowledge (actual: d.144.1.7, sunid 88854) and never confirms it via the API even though the children endpoint would have shown it; the hedge that it is unverified does not make the stated family correct, so must_include 1 is only partly met. Superfamily homology, mechanism, and the refusal to transfer substrate specificity or regulation are well argued; required evidence (kinetics, substrate-bound structures, mutagenesis, partner assays, within-family phylogeny) is listed. Wrong family identifier lowers factual support. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
